purpose: Compare the locally added deployment BFGS post-process with the public UniAD CasADi/IPOPT CollisionNonlinearOptimizer and run a 3x3 raw-trajectory/occupancy cross-ablation.

public_code_contract.python_grid_coordinate_semantics: torch.nonzero returns int64 and the public planning_head.py writes metric grid-center values back into that tensor, truncating toward zero
public_code_contract.public_cpp_sample_collision_correction: not implemented; README and post_process.hpp expose raw trajectory only

solver_only_box_col_difference_percent.definition: IPOPT with floating grid centers minus deployment BFGS with the same floating grid centers

conclusion: The custom BFGS solver is not the cause of the FP16 collision regression. Public-Python integer grid semantics change absolute metrics but FP16 remains anomalous. Holding raw trajectory fixed, FP16 occupancy produces about 0.432-0.438 percent box collision for every raw precision, while FP32 and INT8 occupancy produce about 0.213-0.238 percent. The regression is therefore localized to the collision-sensitive spatial distribution of FP16 occupancy, not global occupancy IoU or raw planning precision.
